Cut off the crusts and slice into fingers.Slingshot gruyère puffs with hot honeyDennis and his slingshotHow to make itAs written, serves 4Crisp little choux puffs loaded with gruyère and cracked pepper, baked hollow and hit with a drizzle of chilli honey and flaky salt.Pocket-sized ammo.Bring 250ml water and 100g butter to the boil, beat in 150g plain flour until it leaves the sides, then cool 5 minutes.Beat in 4 eggs one at a time, then 100g grated gruyere and cracked pepper.Pipe 30 small balls onto lined trays and bake at 200°C for 20 minutes until puffed and hollow.Warm 3 tbsp honey with a pinch of chilli flakes, drizzle over and finish with sea salt.MainsMr Wilson's lamb chops with mint sauceGrilled rosemary lamb chops, mashed potatoes, peas and mint sauceHow to make it8 lamb loin chops1 tbsp chopped rosemary3 garlic cloves, crushed1 tsp salt800g potatoes, peeled and chopped40g butter500g frozen peas4 tbsp mint sauceRub the chops with rosemary, garlic and salt.Boil the potatoes until soft, drain and mash with the butter.Grill the chops, 3 minutes a side, then rest. Cook the peas.Serve everything with a spoon of mint sauce, in peace, with no interruptions at all.Switchblade Sam's campfire snagsDennis at the campfire with Switchblade SamHow to make itAs written, serves 4Thick pork snags charred over the fire, in toasted rolls with sticky caramelised onions, smoky mustard mayo and crunchy pickles.Slice 3 onions and cook slowly in 30g butter with 1 tbsp brown sugar for 25 minutes until sticky and dark.Mix 4 tbsp mayonnaise with 1 tbsp wholegrain mustard and half a tsp smoked paprika.Grill 8 thick pork sausages over medium coals or a barbecue for 15 minutes, turning, until charred and cooked through.Toast 8 long rolls, spread with the mayo and fill with sausages, onions and sliced dill pickles.SweetsMrs Wilson's apple pieLattice-top apple pie with cinnamon, served warmHow to make it6 green apples, peeled and sliced50g butter100g brown sugar1 tsp ground cinnamon3 sheets of shortcrust pastry1 L vanilla ice creamCook the apples with the butter, sugar and cinnamon until just soft, then cool.Line a pie dish with 2 sheets of pastry, fill, and cut the last sheet into strips for a lattice.Bake at 190°C for 45 minutes. Serve warm with ice cream.Mrs Wilson's cookiesOat cookies with dark chocolate chips, golden at the edgesHow to make it125g butter, soft150g brown sugar1 tsp vanilla extract1 egg150g plain flour100g rolled oats150g dark chocolate chipsCream the butter, sugar and vanilla, then beat in the egg. Fold in the flour, oats and chocolate chips.Roll into balls and bake at 180°C until golden at the edges.Cool on the tray for 5 minutes.DrinksBackyard lemonadeFresh lemonade over ice with a halved strawberry in each glassHow to make it150g caster sugar150ml hot water6 lemons, juiced1.5 L cold water4 strawberries, halved1 bag iceDissolve the sugar in the hot water and cool.Juice the lemons into a jug, add the syrup and cold water and stir.Pour into tall glasses over ice and drop a halved strawberry into each.
